label: v as the first input token (t=0)
explanation: Fires when the token v is input at step 0 (first original token), at near-constant magnitude ~1.076 (max). Also a tiny ~0.05 activation when v is input at t=1 right after a leading k (0.1% of mass). Never fires on v at later positions, on other tokens, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase.

issues: Only gap: the predicate leaves out the weak secondary case where v is the input at t=1 right after a leading k (activation about 0.05 of max). On the test split that is 519 missed steps, 3% of activations and 0.15% of activation mass. The explanation already describes this case, and it is fully systematic: '(t==1)&(in_tok==v)&(orig(0)==k)' has precision 1.0 on its own. Adding it as a clause gives test F1 1.0.

Every other claim holds. The feature is 100% in the original phase and 0 in the delimiter and copy phases. Activations only appear at t=0 and t=1. The only input token it fires on is v. Median and max are both 1.076, so the magnitude at t=0 is near-constant. The base predicate has test precision 1.0 with zero false positives.
